verdict: OK to lend in Morbi glass and glassware at or above the 65 threshold, but only to units with verified gas-cost pass-through and clean working-capital cycles; avoid sub-scale units already squeezed by gas prices.
title: Morbi Glass & Glassware: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Morbi glass and glassware runs on furnaces that melt sand and cullet into containers, tableware and processed glass, then form, anneal and pack. **The cash engine is a continuous furnace that must run 24x7, so gas is the single biggest swing cost and the plant cannot be switched off cheaply.** Value sits in the melt and the mould, not the sand; pricing power is thin because buyers are traders and packers who compare quotes daily. Working capital is inventory-heavy (cullet, finished stock) plus receivables from trade channels; capex is furnace rebuilds and forming lines. Collect from customer the exact gas share of cost and the furnace age.

## What has changed now
Local reporting says 50 ceramic units have shut and gas prices crossed 98 [3], and a Morbi Today headline puts propane at 104 per kg from today [2]. **Input cost is moving against the industry right now, and the local press is about ceramics, not glass specifically.** The minister's visit to a Morbi factory and assurance of early resolution of ceramic-industry issues [1][2] is political signalling, not a demand fact. Peer Borosil shows the pattern: Q1 FY2027 revenue up 9% but EBITDA margin down to 14.6% on input inflation, with management targeting 18% via price hikes and solar savings [7]. So when a proposal lands, check whether the unit has actually raised prices; if it has not, ask why and get the price list.

## Where the growth is
Gujarat GST collections are running +11.9% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D], and IIP for NIC 23 is +11.4% YoY [D]. **Pursue Morbi units selling branded tableware and microwave-safe glassware into the domestic lunchbox and storage market, where Borosil cites an INR 4,000 crore lunchbox market with growing demand [5].** Also pursue BIS-compliant container makers and units adding solar power to cut gas exposure, as Borosil is doing with INR 27-28 crore of solar savings at EBITDA level in FY 2027 [4]. Avoid sub-scale job-work furnaces with no brand and no price list.

## How to grow safely
Structure term debt to furnace life, not to a generic tenor, and keep working-capital limits tight against stock statements. **Take monthly: gas price paid per kg, production in tonnes, sales value, and receivable days.** Covenant a minimum EBITDA margin and a maximum gas-cost share of revenue; if gas crosses the level at which the unit's margin falls below covenant, ask for a price-hike proof or reduce exposure. Peer capex is heavy (Borosil INR 125-150 crore FY 2027 [4]), so do not fund expansion on hope of margin recovery.

## Early-warning signs
- Gas price per kg (weekly): a fresh jump with no matching price hike -> freeze new limits and reprice.
- Receivable days (monthly): stretching beyond agreed level -> ask for buyer-wise ageing and stop fresh bills discounting.
- Furnace downtime or rebuild delay (event): -> inspect and reassess term-debt tenor.
- Power/solar commissioning status (quarterly): slippage -> ask for revised cash flow.
watch: crosses the level that breaks covenant margin -> freeze new limits, seek price-hike proof
stretches beyond agreed cap -> demand buyer-wise ageing, halt fresh discounting
unplanned shutdown or rebuild slip -> site inspection, reassess tenor
volume falls while stock rises -> cut working-capital limit
